n.0: The microscope improves visibility but does not itself isolate the tooth.
n.1: The apex locator measures canal length rather than maintaining asepsis.
n.3: Files prepare the canals but do not provide isolation.
n.4: Item 6 shows treatment in progress but the specific isolation device is item 4.

4.q: A patient accidentally overpays at reception and does not notice. What is the most ethical action?
o: Apply the overpayment as credit against future treatment
Hold the amount and refund it if the patient asks
Inform the patient and correct the payment
Record it in the day book and raise it at the month end
Refund it to the card without telling the patient
4.w: Ethical practice requires honesty, fairness and correcting financial errors promptly.

n.0: Decides on the patient's behalf what happens to their money.
n.1: Relies on the patient noticing an error that was ours.
n.3: Recording is right; the delay is not.
n.4: Corrects the money but leaves an unexplained transaction on their statement.

4.q: A dentist instructs a patient to improve cleaning between adjacent teeth to prevent caries formation. Which surfaces are most relevant?
4.w: Mesial and distal surfaces are proximal surfaces where adjacent teeth contact and plaque often accumulates.

n.2: Labial and lingual surfaces are external surfaces, not between teeth.
n.4: Occlusal surfaces are chewing surfaces, not contact points.
n.0: Buccal and occlusal surfaces are not proximal contact areas.
n.1: Incisal and buccal surfaces are not adjacent contact areas.

4.q: Which feature visible in the image is most indicative of a modifiable risk factor for periodontal disease?
4.w: Smoking is a modifiable risk factor clearly demonstrated in the image and significantly impacts periodontal health.

n.4: Tooth morphology is not modifiable.
n.1: Genetic predisposition cannot be modified.
n.0: Age-related changes are non-modifiable.
n.2: Salivary composition is not easily modified in this context.

4.q: A practice is planning a new decontamination room. Which layout principle best supports an effective decontamination workflow?
o: Clean and dirty benches sharing a single sink
Instruments returning along the route they arrived on
Packing carried out next to the wash sink for speed
Storage positioned between the wash and inspection areas
4.w: A one-way progression from dirty to clean areas helps reduce recontamination risks.

n.0: A shared sink is a direct route for contamination to cross zones.
n.2: Backtracking is exactly what a one-way flow is designed to prevent.
n.3: Puts clean packing inside the splash zone.
n.4: Places sterile stock in the middle of the dirty-to-clean route.

4.q: A radiograph of the lower right posterior region shows an unexposed white area along the left side of the image. What is the most likely cause of this appearance?
o: Cone cut due to incorrect beam alignment
Overexposure caused by excessive exposure time
4.w: A sharply defined white unexposed area at the image margin is characteristic of cone cut, caused when the x-ray beam is not centred fully over the receptor.

n.3: Overexposure darkens the whole image rather than creating a localised white border.
n.4: A reversed receptor usually shows herringbone or reduced density, not a clean white margin.
n.2: Movement blur causes loss of sharpness, not a sharply outlined unexposed area.
n.1: Elongation alters tooth length and shape rather than producing a white side border.

4.q: A nurse is preparing to move clinical waste to the external store. Which action best supports staff safety during waste handling?
o: Opening bags to check contents manually
Using suitable PPE and hand hygiene
4.w: Appropriate PPE and hand hygiene help reduce contamination risks.

n.2: Damaged PPE should be replaced.
n.0: Eating during waste handling is inappropriate.
n.1: This increases contamination risk.
n.3: Manual inspection of bags is unsafe.

4.q: What is the most likely interpretation of the exposed root surfaces shown in the image?
4.w: Exposed root surfaces in this context indicate apical migration of the gingival margin and loss of periodontal support.

n.2: Enamel hypoplasia is a developmental enamel defect and does not explain root exposure from gingival recession.
n.4: Normal eruption does not present as inflammatory recession with visible calculus deposits.
n.0: Trauma may cause local injury but would not explain the wider chronic periodontal features.
n.1: A supernumerary tooth is unrelated to the recession and periodontal changes shown.

4.q: Which numbered item shows the materials most likely to include irrigants and endodontic consumables used chairside during treatment?
4.w: Item 1 shows a tray containing consumables and solutions likely used for endodontic procedures, including irrigants and accessory items.

n.1: Item 2 is the operating microscope, which assists vision rather than supplying irrigants.
n.2: Item 3 is an apex locator.
n.3: Item 4 is rubber dam isolation equipment.
n.4: Item 5 is mainly the file and accessory set rather than the tray of liquids and consumables.

5.q: A cycle finishes and the display shows a pass. Which record should be completed immediately after a successful cycle?
5.w: The steriliser log should be completed to maintain traceable processing records.

n.0: Holiday requests are unrelated.
n.2: Reception diaries are not decontamination records.
n.4: Uniform checks do not document cycles.
n.1: Invoices are unrelated to sterilisation.

5.q: A patient sips sugary fizzy drinks throughout the afternoon. What is the best dietary advice?
o: Switch to a wider straw only
5.w: Reducing frequency of sugar exposure and keeping sugary drinks to mealtimes helps lower caries risk.

n.4: A straw may reduce contact slightly but does not address frequent sugar intake.
n.3: More frequent sipping increases repeated sugar attacks.
n.0: Brushing after every sip is impractical and does not address intake pattern.
n.1: Holding drinks in the mouth increases exposure time.

5.q: A patient is not breathing normally and rescue breaths are required. Which item is most appropriate basic equipment to assist ventilation during a medical emergency?
5.w: A pocket mask is designed to help deliver rescue breaths more safely during resuscitation.

n.2: An impression tray is not used for ventilation.
n.0: A cheek retractor does not provide assisted ventilation.
n.1: An endodontic ruler is unrelated to airway support.
n.4: A wax knife has no emergency airway function.

5.q: A practice wants to reduce the risk of processed packs becoming recontaminated. Which practice best protects the clean zone?
5.w: A dedicated clean storage area helps keep sterilised items separate from contamination sources.

n.2: Shared cloths may spread contamination.
n.3: Used trays should stay in dirty zones.
n.4: Waste should be separated from clean stock.
n.1: Opening packs early removes barrier protection.

5.q: Boxes and wrappers are left over after restocking the surgery. Which waste item is most suitable for general domestic waste if uncontaminated?
5.w: Clean uncontaminated paper packaging may enter the appropriate domestic/recycling stream depending on policy.

n.4: Needles are sharps.
n.1: Bloodied gauze requires clinical waste segregation.
n.3: Biological waste requires specific handling.
n.0: Amalgam waste requires controlled disposal.

5.q: During treatment, a patient suddenly becomes pale, sweaty and says they feel faint after seeing the local anaesthetic needle. What is the most likely emergency being recognised?
5.w: Pallor, sweating and feeling faint triggered by anxiety are classic features of vasovagal syncope.

n.0: Asthma usually presents with wheeze, breathlessness and chest tightness.
n.2: Seizure would more commonly involve altered consciousness or convulsive activity.
n.3: Hyperglycaemia develops more gradually and commonly causes thirst or lethargy.
n.1: Anaphylaxis often includes airway, breathing or skin changes after exposure.

5.q: Used items have been returned from surgery but not yet processed. Which item should remain in the dirty zone until processed?
5.w: Used hand instruments are contaminated and belong in the dirty zone until decontaminated.

n.0: Labels are not contaminated instruments.
n.4: Wrapped cassettes may be clean processed stock.
n.1: Sterile packs belong in the clean zone.
n.2: Administrative sheets are not dirty-zone items.

5.q: A patient attends with a tongue ulcer that has been present for over 3 weeks and has not improved. What is the most appropriate action by the dental team?
o: Advise salt mouthrinses and review in 6 months
Polish the adjacent teeth and discharge the patient
Prescribe antibiotics as the main treatment
Reassure the patient that all tongue ulcers are harmless
Record the finding and arrange urgent referral for further assessment
5.w: A persistent ulcer present for more than 3 weeks requires urgent referral for assessment because oral cancer must be excluded.

n.0: A 6-month delay is inappropriate for a suspicious lesion.
n.1: Removing local factors may help in some cases, but a persistent lesion still requires urgent assessment.
n.2: Antibiotics are not the primary management for a suspicious persistent oral ulcer.
n.3: Persistent tongue ulcers are not all harmless and should not be dismissed.

5.q: A patient's social history is being recorded before an oral cancer screening. Which combination of risk factors most significantly increases the likelihood of oral cancer?
o: Low sugar intake and fluoride use
5.w: Smoking and alcohol together significantly increase the risk of oral cancer due to their synergistic effects.

n.2: These are not risk factors for oral cancer.
n.1: These are protective behaviours.
n.0: These do not increase cancer risk.
n.3: These are beneficial for oral health.

5.q: An old metal restoration has been removed and collected in the suction trap. Which item most likely requires specialist disposal rather than standard clinical waste?
5.w: Amalgam waste requires specialist disposal due to mercury content and environmental controls.

n.3: Paper bibs may enter another stream depending on contamination.
n.2: Wrappers are not specialist hazardous waste.
n.1: Clean cardboard is not specialist waste.
n.4: Cup lids are not specialist waste.

5.q: During placement of a composite restoration, the patient closes unexpectedly while instruments are in the mouth. What is the best action?
o: Ask the patient to keep their mouth open and continue
Complete the increment being cured before stopping
Increase suction and continue with a mouth prop in place
Reassure the patient and let the operator decide whether to stop
Withdraw instruments safely and check the patient
5.w: Immediate safe removal of instruments and checking for injury is the priority.

n.0: Does not check whether closing has caused any injury.
n.1: Prioritises the restoration over the patient's safety.
n.2: A prop helps prevent a recurrence, but only after checking for injury.
n.3: Instruments should be made safe first, not while a decision is discussed.

5.q: A patient swaps from fizzy cola to sweetened fruit juice and drinks it often. How should this be interpreted?
o: Sweet drinks are equal to water
5.w: Although different from cola, sweetened juice taken frequently may still expose teeth to sugar.

n.2: Juice can still be relevant to oral health advice.
n.0: Risk depends on content and frequency.
n.3: Many sugary drinks can contribute to decay risk.
n.4: Sweet drinks are not equivalent to water.

5.q: A needle must be recapped because treatment is interrupted and it will be reused immediately. What is the best method?
o: Ask patient to hold the cap
Use a safer one-handed or device-assisted method
5.w: If unavoidable, recapping should use a safer one-handed or approved device-assisted technique.

n.3: Two-handed recapping increases injury risk.
n.0: Patients must not assist with sharps handling.
n.1: Bending damages the needle and increases risk.
n.2: Using fingers near the point is unsafe.

5.q: A patient is seated for an extraction and says they are unsure whether they want to continue. What is the best immediate action?
o: Ask the nurse to persuade the patient
Begin local anaesthetic quickly before they change their mind
Pause treatment and inform the dentist so the patient can discuss options
Proceed because the appointment was booked
Tell the patient they must continue
5.w: If a patient expresses uncertainty, treatment should pause so valid consent can be reviewed and the patient can decide freely.

n.3: A booking does not replace valid consent.
n.0: Patients should not be pressured into treatment.
n.1: Starting treatment without clear consent is inappropriate.
n.4: Patients cannot be forced to continue elective treatment.

5.q: Using the image, identify instrument set number 2.
5.w: These are hand instruments used for periodontal scaling and root surface debridement.

n.4: Matrix retainers are used during restorative procedures.
n.2: Luxators are primarily extraction instruments.
n.0: Carvers are used when shaping amalgam restorations.
n.1: Bracket kits are associated with orthodontic treatment.

5.q: A colleague gives a patient conflicting appointment information. What is the best action?
o: Ask the patient which version they would prefer
Book the patient in again to be certain
Correct your colleague in front of the patient
Let the appointment stand and adjust the diary later
5.w: Prompt clarification prevents confusion and maintains confidence.

n.0: Preference does not establish what was actually arranged.
n.1: Creates a duplicate booking and more confusion.
n.3: Undermines the colleague and the patient's confidence.
n.4: Leaves the patient holding information you know to be wrong.

5.q: Which surface of the tooth shown in the image would be most prone to plaque accumulation due to pits and fissures?
5.w: The occlusal surface contains pits and fissures where plaque easily accumulates.

n.0: Buccal surfaces are smoother.
n.2: Lingual surfaces generally lack deep fissures.
n.3: Mesial surfaces are contact areas.
n.1: Distal surfaces are also contact areas.

5.q: A dentist identifies tooth 14 for treatment. What is the best action for the dental nurse?
o: Prepare for lower left first premolar treatment
Prepare for lower right first premolar treatment
Prepare for upper left first premolar treatment
Prepare for upper right first premolar treatment
Prepare for upper right second premolar treatment
5.w: Tooth 14 is in quadrant 1 (upper right) and position 4 (first premolar).

n.2: Upper left first premolar would be 24.
n.1: Lower right first premolar would be 44.
n.4: Upper right second premolar would be 15.
n.0: Lower left first premolar would be 34.

5.q: Using the image, identify item number 4.
5.w: Item 4 is a sterile drape used to maintain an aseptic field.

n.0: A bib clip is metallic and much smaller.
n.4: Tray liners are usually fitted inside trays.
n.2: Headrest covers are shaped differently.
n.1: Disposable napkins are not intended as sterile drapes.

5.q: Based on the image provided, which structure is the outermost protective layer of the crown?
5.w: Enamel is the highly mineralised outer layer of the crown that provides protection.

n.1: Dentine lies beneath enamel and is not the outermost layer.
n.4: The pulp chamber is internal.
n.0: Cementum covers the root, not the crown.
n.3: The periodontal ligament supports the tooth within bone.

5.q: A patient has central chest pain not relieved by their own GTN spray and looks clammy. What is the best management?
o: Ask the patient to drive home and rest
Call emergency services and manage as possible myocardial infarction
Continue treatment but shorten the appointment
Place them in the recovery position immediately
5.w: Persistent chest pain with systemic symptoms may indicate myocardial infarction and requires urgent escalation.

n.2: Continuing treatment delays urgent care.
n.3: Glucose does not treat suspected cardiac chest pain.
n.0: The patient should not self-transport in this situation.
n.4: Recovery position is not first-line for a conscious chest pain patient.

5.q: A tray of used instruments has been through the washer-disinfector. Which sequence is most appropriate before instruments enter the steriliser?
5.w: Instruments should be cleaned, inspected, packaged where required, then loaded for sterilisation.

n.4: Cleaning should occur before packaging.
n.1: Inspection occurs before sterilisation.
n.2: Use must not occur before decontamination.
n.3: Cleaning must happen before loading.

5.q: A patient complains of sharp pain when consuming cold drinks, but no spontaneous pain. What stage is most likely?
5.w: Sharp sensitivity suggests dentine involvement without pulpal inflammation.

n.3: Necrosis typically results in no sensation.
n.1: Enamel caries may not cause sensitivity.
n.2: Periodontal disease presents differently.
n.4: Fracture would show structural damage.

5.q: A yellow bag in the surgery contains blood-contaminated gauze and used PPE. What is the best action?
o: Dispose of it in the correct clinical waste stream
Empty it into a black sack
Store it under the sink indefinitely
5.w: Waste contaminated with blood or body fluids should be segregated into the correct clinical waste stream according to local policy.

n.3: Domestic waste is inappropriate for contaminated clinical waste.
n.1: Clinical waste should not be decanted into another general sack.
n.4: Waste should not be stored indefinitely.
n.2: Contaminated waste must not enter recycling streams.

5.q: Item 2 in the image is being prepared for use with a light-body impression material. What should be done before clinical use?
o: Cool the cartridge on the glass slab for several minutes
Express a small amount first to ensure even flow from both pastes
Place it immediately into the mouth before attaching the tip
Remove the mixing tip once the material starts flowing
Shake the cartridge vigorously after seating the tray
5.w: Bleeding a small amount first helps confirm both base and catalyst are flowing correctly before the mixing tip is used.

n.2: The tip must be attached and the material prepared properly before intraoral use.
n.4: Shaking after tray seating is inappropriate and risks inaccuracy.
n.3: Removing the tip during use would disrupt mixing and waste material.
n.0: Cooling the cartridge on a slab is not the standard step here.

5.q: The pointed upward extension of the mandibular ramus located anterior to the condyle is the:
5.w: The coronoid process is the anterior superior projection of the mandibular ramus and may be visible on panoramic radiographs.

n.2: Genial tubercles are midline mandibular structures behind lower incisors.
n.0: The articular eminence is part of the temporal bone near the TMJ.
n.4: The zygomatic process belongs to the maxilla or temporal bone, depending on context.
n.3: The lingula is a small internal mandibular landmark near the mandibular foramen.

5.q: An orthodontist requires assessment of jaw relationships and incisor inclination. Based on the image shown, which type of radiograph has been taken?
5.w: The image is a side-view skull projection showing facial profile, jaws and dentition, characteristic of a lateral cephalometric radiograph.

n.2: A panoramic radiograph shows both jaws in a curved frontal view, not a side skull projection.
n.4: Bitewings are small intraoral views of posterior crowns.
n.3: Periapicals are localised intraoral images of selected teeth and apices.
n.1: A lower occlusal radiograph shows the mandibular arch from above.

5.q: Which numbered item would most likely be selected when the operator asks for a saliva ejector tip?
5.w: Item 4 shows aspirator tips used to remove saliva and fluids during treatment.

n.0: Item 1 is a mixed tray setup rather than the suction tip requested.
n.1: Item 2 contains examination instruments.
n.3: Item 5 is a rubber dam punch.
n.4: Item 6 contains matrix accessories.

5.q: A patient has been seated for the removal of an upper premolar. Before a routine extraction begins, what is the most important first check by the dental nurse?
5.w: Correct patient identification is a fundamental safety requirement before treatment starts.

n.1: Polishing paste shade is unrelated to oral surgery.
n.0: Impression trays are not the first priority.
n.4: Study casts are not required initially.
n.3: Whitening gel is unrelated.

5.q: A patient reports relief of pain after a period of severe toothache, followed by swelling. What does this indicate?
5.w: Pain relief followed by swelling suggests pulp necrosis and abscess formation.

n.0: Pulp does not heal after severe infection.
n.3: Caries does not resolve spontaneously.
n.1: This is not related to hygiene improvement.
n.4: Remineralisation does not occur at this stage.

5.q: Which numbered item is used to place holes accurately into a rubber dam sheet before isolation?
5.w: Item 5 is the rubber dam punch, used to create correctly sized holes in the dam sheet.

n.0: Item 1 is a tray arrangement rather than the specific punching instrument.
n.1: Item 2 contains hand instruments used intra-orally.
n.2: Item 4 shows suction tips for moisture control.
n.4: Item 6 contains clamps, bands and wedges.

5.q: Using the image, identify the instrument most suited for removing subgingival deposits.
5.w: Curettes are designed for subgingival scaling and root debridement.

n.0: An amalgam carrier transports restorative material.
n.4: A mouth prop assists opening, not scaling.
n.3: Luxators are extraction instruments.
n.1: Burnishers contour restorations.

5.q: A patient asks why their gums bleed even though they do not feel pain. Which is the best response?
o: Bleeding is a sign of gingival inflammation, even when there is no pain
Bleeding is caused by enamel erosion
Bleeding is expected if teeth are brushed correctly
Bleeding means the teeth are about to exfoliate naturally
Bleeding only happens when the pulp is infected
5.w: Gingival inflammation commonly causes bleeding without pain, especially in plaque-induced periodontal disease.

n.4: Pulp infection is not required for gingival bleeding to occur.
n.3: Bleeding does not mean the teeth will naturally exfoliate.
n.2: Bleeding is not an expected sign of effective healthy brushing.
n.1: Enamel erosion does not directly cause gingival bleeding.

5.q: A student states that this radiograph can replace bitewings for detecting early interproximal caries. What is the most appropriate response?
o: Correct, because panoramic radiographs show all tooth surfaces clearly
Correct, because they eliminate image distortion
Correct, because they provide higher resolution than bitewings
Incorrect, because panoramic radiographs cannot show posterior teeth
Incorrect, because panoramic radiographs lack sufficient detail for early caries detection
5.w: Panoramic radiographs have lower resolution and are not suitable for detecting early interproximal caries compared to bitewings.

n.0: Panoramic radiographs do not show fine detail of tooth surfaces clearly.
n.2: Bitewings provide higher resolution for caries detection.
n.3: Panoramic radiographs do show posterior teeth.
n.1: Panoramic images are subject to distortion, not free from it.

5.q: A patient with visible plaque accumulation asks what contributes most to their gum disease. Which is the best response?
o: Calculus is the direct cause of the inflammation
Diet has the greatest influence on gum disease
Plaque bacteria are the primary cause, influenced by risk factors
Smoking is the main cause in most patients
The body's immune response alone determines the damage
5.w: Plaque bacteria are the primary cause of periodontal disease, with risk factors such as smoking influencing severity.

n.0: Calculus retains plaque and makes cleaning harder, but the plaque bacteria drive the disease.
n.1: Diet is central to caries; its role in periodontal disease is much smaller.
n.3: A major risk factor that worsens disease, but not the cause of it.
n.4: The host response shapes the damage, but only once plaque bacteria are present.

5.q: Interpret the clinical findings in the image. What feature indicates disease progression?
5.w: Heavy calculus deposits contribute to plaque retention and disease progression.

n.0: Firm gingiva is a sign of health.
n.1: Stippling is associated with healthy gingiva.
n.2: Pale pink colour indicates health, not disease.
n.4: Shallow sulcus depth is not indicative of progression.

5.q: During instrument clean-down, a used local anaesthetic needle is found on the tray. What is the safest immediate action?
o: Ask the person who used it to dispose of it when they return
Carry it in a kidney dish to the sharps bin in the next room
Place it directly into an approved sharps container at the point of use
Re-sheath it using a single-handed scoop technique before disposal
Separate the needle from the syringe using a needle remover first
5.w: Used sharps should be disposed of immediately into an approved sharps container as close as possible to where they are used.

n.0: Responsibility does sit with the user, but leaving an exposed needle on a tray creates a hazard now.
n.1: Transporting an exposed sharp adds handling and risk; the bin should come to the sharp.
n.3: The scoop technique is safer than two hands, but re-sheathing at all is avoided where a bin is available.
n.4: Adds an unnecessary manipulation of a contaminated needle.

5.q: Item 10 in the image is laid out before mixing zinc phosphate cement. What type of item is it?
5.w: Item 10 is a glass slab used as a cool mixing surface for certain dental cements and pastes.

n.3: A rubber mixing bowl is used more commonly for materials such as alginate.
n.1: A dappen dish is a small container for holding small amounts of liquid or material.
n.4: A sterilisation cassette stores instruments for processing and transport.
n.0: An acrylic denture flask is laboratory equipment used in denture processing.

5.q: An AED advises a shock. What is the best action immediately before pressing the shock button?
o: Ensure nobody is touching the patient
Remove both pads and dry the chest again
5.w: Before shock delivery, everyone must be clear of contact with the patient for safety and effective shock administration.

n.2: Do not delay a prompted shock to give breaths.
n.4: If a shock is advised, it should be delivered promptly.
n.3: Pads should remain in place unless incorrectly attached.
n.0: A prolonged pulse check delays defibrillation.

5.q: Using the image, which item appears incorrectly positioned within the decontamination workflow?
5.w: Sterile packs should be separated from dirty instruments and dirty workflow areas.

n.0: Wall-mounted gloves are not the key workflow error shown.
n.3: Soap near a sink is appropriate.
n.2: Sharps bins may be side-positioned if safely located.
n.1: Hand rub height is not the main sterilisation workflow issue.

5.q: The tooth shown with a blue sheet and clamp arrangement is isolated using which method?
5.w: The clamp and blue sheet indicate rubber dam isolation, commonly used during restorative procedures for moisture control.

n.1: Cotton rolls do not involve a clamp and stretched sheet.
n.4: A saliva ejector alone would not provide this level of isolation.
n.0: Cheek retractors do not isolate a single tooth in this way.
n.2: High-volume suction assists but does not create the shown barrier.

5.q: A patient smokes heavily and presents with periodontal disease. What effect does smoking have?
o: Reduces inflammation signs but worsens disease
5.w: Smoking masks inflammation but accelerates periodontal destruction.

n.1: Smoking impairs healing.
n.2: Smoking does not prevent plaque.
n.4: Smoking weakens tissues.
n.0: Smoking does not eliminate bacteria.

5.q: A local anaesthetic cartridge and needle have just been used. Which sequence best reflects safe sharps disposal after use?
o: Carry needle to desk, then bin
Dispose immediately at point of use
Leave on tray until surgery ends
5.w: Sharps should be disposed of promptly into an approved container as close to point of use as possible.

n.0: Unnecessary transport increases injury risk.
n.2: Leaving sharps on trays is unsafe.
n.3: Passing uncovered sharps increases risk.
n.4: Carrying sharps in clothing is unsafe.

5.q: A staff member lifts a heavy stock box by twisting quickly. What should be recognised as the main risk?
o: Musculoskeletal injury from poor manual handling
5.w: Poor lifting technique increases the risk of back and other musculoskeletal injuries.

n.2: Paper cuts are not the main risk described.
n.4: Cleanliness is unrelated.
n.0: Stock rotation is unrelated.
n.3: Lighting quality is irrelevant.

5.q: Ultrasonic scaling is under way on a patient with heavy subgingival deposits. If blood and saliva obscure the working field during scaling, what should the nurse do first?
5.w: Effective suction improves visibility and moisture control during periodontal treatment.

n.4: Turning off the light reduces visibility.
n.3: Removing the bib does not help control fluids.
n.0: Shade guides are irrelevant.
n.1: Opening packs does not solve the immediate issue.

5.q: A nurse is auditing sterilised stock in the clean store. Which error should be recognised when dating sterilised packs?
5.w: Missing the processing date weakens traceability and stock control.

n.3: Legible labels are good practice.
n.0: Batch coding supports traceability.
n.4: Clear writing is desirable.
n.1: Stock rotation checks are appropriate.

5.q: Item 10 in the image is laid out before mixing a luting cement. How should this item be classified?
5.w: Item 10 is a glass slab used as a cool mixing surface for certain cements and pastes.

n.0: A dappen dish is a small container, usually circular and deeper.
n.2: An instrument cassette lid is part of a sterilisation container.
n.3: An occlusal registration plate is not used as a mixing surface.
n.4: A bur block is designed to hold rotary instruments.

5.q: A patient has arrived for a planned appointment and is waiting in reception. Which sequence best reflects good patient management when escorting someone into the surgery?
o: Ask for payment, then check name
Confirm identity, welcome them, explain what happens next
Leave them standing while preparing instruments
Seat them first, identify later, explain nothing
5.w: Checking identity, welcoming the patient and explaining the next steps supports safe, respectful care.

n.3: Identity should be confirmed before proceeding.
n.4: Treatment should not begin before appropriate introduction and checks.
n.0: Administrative matters do not replace identity checks.
n.2: Leaving patients unsupported may reduce confidence.

5.q: A patient undergoes this radiographic examination. Which sequence best describes the process of acquiring this image?
o: Insert film parallel to tooth → direct beam perpendicular → expose image
Place film on occlusal surface → direct beam vertically → expose image
Place sensor intraorally → align X-ray beam → expose image
Position patient → rotate X-ray source and detector around the head → capture composite image
Position receptor behind tooth → bisect angle → expose image
5.w: Panoramic radiography involves positioning the patient while the X-ray source and detector rotate around the head to produce a composite image of the jaws.

n.2: This describes intraoral radiography such as bitewings or periapicals.
n.0: This describes the paralleling technique for periapical radiographs.
n.1: This describes an occlusal radiograph technique.
n.4: This describes the bisecting angle technique for periapicals.

5.q: Item 11 in the image is selected during contouring of a Class IV composite. What is its most likely use?
o: To adjust a matrix retainer spindle intraorally
To carry amalgam from the capsule into the cavity
To place and shape composite without sticking excessively
To remove soft carious dentine by excavation only
To wedge interproximally before band placement
5.w: A plastic composite instrument is used to place and contour composite material while minimising sticking and distortion.

Restart treatment before asking how they feel
Stand them up immediately and escort them out
9.w: Patients recovering from syncope should be reassessed and returned upright gradually once stable.

n.3: Treatment restart should only follow full recovery and review.
n.0: Adrenaline is not routine for syncope.

9.q: A patient with stroke symptoms is conscious and breathing normally. Which management approach is most appropriate?
o: Ask them to walk to the car for hospital transfer
Call emergency services promptly and monitor airway and responsiveness
Give them oral glucose routinely before assessment
Lay them fully flat and leave them alone

n.3: Glucose is not routinely given without indication.
n.4: Leaving the patient unattended is unsafe.
n.2: Treatment should cease immediately.
n.0: The patient should not self-mobilise or self-transport.

9.q: The curing light tip is visibly coated with composite residue and is used without being cleaned. What error is most likely to result?
o: Excessive etching of the enamel margins
Improved contact point formation in the proximal box
More accurate shade matching under the operating light
Reduced light transmission to the restoration surface
9.w: Residue on the curing light tip can reduce the amount of light reaching the composite, increasing the risk of inadequate curing.

n.1: Contact point formation depends on matrixing and contour, not light-tip cleanliness.
n.3: A contaminated curing light tip does not improve shade matching and may reduce clinical effectiveness.

9.q: A dental chart incorrectly labels the chewing surface of a premolar as the incisal surface. What is the error?
o: Incisal applies only to posterior teeth
Mesial surface was confused with distal

n.2: Lingual omission is not the primary issue.
n.0: Buccal labeling is unrelated to the chewing surface.

9.q: A luting cement is selected because it must form a very thin layer beneath a crown to allow complete seating. Which property is most relevant?

n.2: Surface hardness may matter later but does not primarily determine seating.
n.0: Shade value is not the key requirement under a crown.
n.1: High elasticity is not the principal property sought here.
n.4: Colour change is unrelated to crown seating.

9.q: A patient asks how an untreated cavity ended up causing an abscess. Which sequence best describes progression from caries to abscess?

n.0: Abscess occurs last.
n.1: Enamel is affected first.
n.2: Abscess does not precede pulp involvement.

9.q: A tray of used instruments is placed on the clean packing bench while space is made elsewhere. What is the best action?

Decontaminate the bench around the tray and continue
Move it to the dirty zone immediately
Move the packing work to another bench instead
Place a barrier sheet under the tray and carry on

9.q: A patient with inflamed, bleeding gums asks for home-care advice. Which error in patient advice would be inappropriate for this condition?

Discuss the role of calculus in plaque retention
Explain that bleeding can improve with better plaque control
9.w: Telling a patient to stop brushing bleeding areas is inappropriate because it allows plaque levels to rise and inflammation to persist.

n.2: Interdental cleaning is a useful measure where suitable for the patient.
n.1: Explaining the plaque-retentive role of calculus is appropriate patient education.

9.q: Using the image, which observation indicates poor separation practice?

n.1: Hand rub supports infection control.
n.2: A sharps container is expected.
n.3: Glove holders are normal fixtures.
n.4: Fitted lids are generally appropriate.

9.q: After removing gloves, a clinician immediately answers the phone before hand hygiene. What is the most likely consequence?

n.2: The phone contact is not limited to mask contamination.

n.0: Efficiency does not outweigh contamination risk.

9.q: A student asks how healthy gums become periodontally diseased. Which sequence best describes the pathological progression of periodontal disease?
9.w: Periodontal disease progresses from health to gingivitis and then to periodontitis if untreated.

n.3: Periodontitis does not precede gingivitis.
n.0: Health does not occur between disease stages.
n.4: This is the reverse of the correct progression.
n.1: Health is the starting point, not the end.

9.q: A surgery is running behind and the pre-treatment conversation is cut short. Which behaviour most increases consent-related mistakes in practice?

n.0: Checking understanding reduces mistakes.
n.4: Clear language supports valid consent.
n.1: Time to decide supports autonomy.
n.2: Careful records support good practice.

9.q: A clinical waste bag has reached its fill level at the end of the day. Which sequence is most appropriate for closing a waste bag ready for collection?

Empty contents, retie, refill, leave in surgery
Overfill, drag, tie loosely, store open
Place in corridor, then decide later
Seal first, then add more waste
9.w: The bag should be checked, securely closed, labelled if required and moved to the designated storage area.

n.2: These actions are unsafe and poor practice.
n.1: Reopening and refilling sealed bags is inappropriate.

n.3: Corridors are not suitable temporary storage areas.

9.q: Using the image, which item is primarily intended for sharps segregation?
9.w: The yellow sharps container is designed for safe segregation and disposal of sharps waste.

n.1: Glove dispensers store PPE.
n.3: A sink is not for sharps disposal.

9.q: Dietary advice is being given to a parent of a young child. Which of the following best describes an error in dietary advice for caries prevention?

9.q: During canal irrigation, the nurse notices that sodium hypochlorite has been drawn into an unlabelled syringe. What is the best action?

Discard it safely and replace it with a correctly identified syringe
Keep it separate and rely on memory to identify it
Pass it immediately before there is any confusion
Use it only for the first canal instrument pass

Place lining cement over the area
Proceed with bonding as contamination is harmless
Rinse, dry appropriately and re-etch according to protocol

Continue treatment because symptoms may settle
