n.2: Tea rotas are unrelated.
n.0: Holiday calendars are unrelated.
n.1: Recall lists are unrelated.
n.4: Window cleaning logs are unrelated.

12.q: A nurse repeatedly struggles to put gloves on before appointments. Which observation most strongly suggests gloves are the wrong size?
o: Frequent tearing when donned and restricted movement
12.w: Tearing on donning and poor dexterity commonly indicate incorrect sizing.

n.2: Warmth alone does not indicate size error.
n.3: Powder-free status does not indicate fit.
n.0: Colour is irrelevant.

12.q: The radiography list is running behind and exposures are being taken quickly. Which behaviour most increases IRMER-related mistakes in practice?
o: Rushing and bypassing identification or positioning checks

12.q: During a busy list two identical trays are picked up in the wrong order. What is the best action if clean and dirty trays are accidentally swapped?
o: Continue and keep the trays clearly apart from now on
Re-label the trays and carry on with the session
Treat both trays as clean since neither was opened
Wipe the outside of both trays and continue

n.0: Does nothing about the items whose status is already uncertain.
n.1: A label does not establish which instruments are actually processed.

12.q: Which aspect of interpretation is most affected by the fault seen on this panoramic radiograph?
o: Assessment of root outlines and surrounding bony detail
Counting the number of erupted teeth
Identifying that the image is panoramic
Recognising the presence of the mandible
Seeing that restorations may be present

12.q: The lesion in the image appears cavitated. What does this indicate?
12.w: Cavitation indicates irreversible destruction of tooth structure.

n.3: Cavitation is beyond reversible stages.
n.4: Stains do not involve structural breakdown.
n.0: Fluoride uptake prevents caries.
n.2: Plaque alone does not indicate cavitation.

12.q: A patient attends for review two weeks after new dentures were fitted. Which finding most strongly suggests improved adaptation to new dentures?
o: Fewer ulcers than at the first review
Speech returning to normal within a few days
The denture needing less fixative than before
The patient wearing it for longer each day
12.w: Increasing comfort commonly suggests improving adaptation.

n.1: Encouraging, but ulcers may simply have been adjusted rather than adaptation occurring.
n.2: A good sign, though speech often settles before the denture is truly comfortable.
n.3: Suggests better retention, but fixative use varies with habit as much as fit.
n.4: Increased wear can reflect determination as much as comfort.

12.q: A patient is midway through a course of complete denture construction. Why are jaw relation records taken during complete denture construction?
12.w: Jaw relation records help establish the correct occlusal relationship.

n.1: Pulp vitality is unrelated.
n.0: Implant torque is unrelated here.
n.2: Pocket depths are periodontal records.
n.4: This is unrelated to whitening.

12.q: Several mandibular periapicals in one session show the same long-root appearance as this image. What is the most likely cause?
o: The tubehead is repeatedly positioned with too shallow a vertical angle
12.w: Repeated elongation usually indicates the operator is consistently using insufficient vertical angulation.

n.2: Exhausted chemicals affect density and contrast, not image length.
n.1: Swallowing may create movement blur, not elongation.
n.3: Packet contamination does not create geometric distortion.
n.0: Timer faults alter exposure rather than tooth proportions.

12.q: Which feature in the image confirms that the lesion is active rather than arrested?
12.w: Active lesions are soft, discoloured, and often cavitated.

n.0: Hard surfaces suggest arrested lesions.
n.2: Smooth enamel is healthy.
n.4: Uniform colour indicates no lesion.
n.1: Plaque is typically present in active lesions.

12.q: Which feature in the image indicates chronic rather than acute infection?
12.w: A draining sinus suggests a chronic abscess.

n.2: Redness is seen in both acute and chronic cases.
n.0: Swelling can occur in both.
n.3: Sharp pain is more acute.
n.4: Temperature sensitivity relates to pulpitis.

12.q: A bur is found loose in a drawer. What is the best action?
o: Handle carefully and place it into an appropriate sharps container
Place it in the instrument tray for the next decontamination cycle
Return it to the bur block for reuse after cleaning
Wrap it securely and place it in the clinical waste bag
Wrap it securely and place it in the offensive waste stream

n.2: Its history is unknown, so it cannot be assumed safe to reuse.
n.3: Clinical waste bags offer no puncture protection; sharps need a rigid container.
n.4: Wrong waste stream, and again no protection against puncture.

12.q: The surgery is being prepared for a session of ultrasonic scaling. When setting up for ultrasonic periodontal treatment, what should be checked first?
12.w: Adequate water flow is required for cooling and lavage.

n.3: Shade tabs are unrelated.
n.2: A model trimmer is a laboratory item.
n.0: Articulators are unrelated.
n.1: Impression trays are not required.

12.q: A dental nurse incorrectly tells a patient that caries only affects enamel. Why is this incorrect?
o: Caries affects enamel, dentine, and can reach the pulp
12.w: Caries progresses from enamel into dentine and potentially the pulp.

n.4: Caries begins in enamel.
n.2: Gums are not directly affected.
n.3: Caries is progressive.
n.0: Bone is not directly affected.

12.q: Interpret the gingival condition shown in the image.
12.w: Redness and bleeding indicate inflammation caused by plaque.

n.2: Healthy tissue is not inflamed.
n.0: No evidence of trauma is present.
n.1: Allergic reactions present differently.
n.4: No signs of neoplasia are visible.

12.q: The practice is running late and the surgery is being cleared quickly. Which behaviour most increases waste disposal errors in a busy practice?
12.w: Rushing often leads to shortcuts and incorrect waste segregation.

n.1: Clear signage helps reduce errors.
n.2: Training supports compliance.
n.0: Enough bins reduces misuse.
n.3: Audits help identify issues.

12.q: A spill of developer solution occurs on the floor. What is the best immediate response?
o: Absorb it with paper towels and place them in domestic waste
Dilute it with plenty of water and mop the area
Follow the spill procedure using appropriate controls
Isolate the area and wait for the next scheduled clean
Ventilate the room and allow the spill to evaporate
12.w: Chemical spills should be managed promptly using local spill procedures and suitable controls.

n.0: Contaminated absorbent goes into the correct hazardous stream, not domestic waste.
n.1: Spreads the chemical over a larger area and into the drainage system.

12.q: Which sequence is most appropriate to avoid the coverage error seen on this image?
o: Angle the tubehead more steeply, then expose without repositioning
Expose first, then decide whether the molar was included
Increase exposure time, then move the receptor backwards
Place receptor further posteriorly, align holder, confirm tooth coverage, then expose
Process the image before checking posterior positioning

n.2: Exposure time does not correct placement errors.
n.4: Processing occurs after exposure and does not prevent positioning faults.
n.0: Tubehead angulation alone does not reliably correct posterior exclusion.

12.q: Item 5 in the image is being prepared before etching enamel. Which instrument type is it?

n.0: An amalgam carrier transfers triturated amalgam into a cavity.
n.1: An aspirating syringe is for local anaesthetic administration.
n.2: An endodontic irrigating cannula is used for canal irrigation.
n.4: A three-in-one syringe delivers air and water from the dental unit.

12.q: A matrix band is being placed for a Class II amalgam restoration. Which sequence is correct?
o: Apply bonding agent, then fit matrix band only
Insert wedge, select shade, etch enamel, tighten retainer, burnish
Mix amalgam, wedge first, then choose band size
Place retainer, remove band, wedge later, cure light, polish
Select band, place retainer, adapt band, insert wedge, tighten

n.2: Material should not be mixed before proper matrix preparation.
n.0: Bonding agent is not part of routine amalgam matrix placement.

12.q: A colleague's eyewear keeps misting up during treatment. Which observation most strongly suggests a mask is poorly fitted?
o: Air escapes upward causing repeated fogging of eyewear
The mask matches the uniform colour

n.3: Colour matching is irrelevant.
n.4: Strap colour does not indicate fit.
